stumbles.quote: Jev had done well on routing questions, so I was hopeful.
stumbles.why: Refers to prior Jev work on routing questions that the text never describes; the reader doesn't know what that was or why it predicts success here.

stumbles.quote: With the tic's definition from register.md in its prompt
stumbles.why: 'The tic' and register.md are never explained. The reader doesn't know what a tic is, which tic is meant, or what register.md contains.
'Real tics' is undefined. It's also unclear whether Jev was scored only on the 261 agreed hits or on all 300, and the table counts (44+43+18 = 105) are not tied to this set.

stumbles.quote: at a 5% error budget it could settle only 24.5% of hits
stumbles.why: 'Settle' and 'error budget' are not defined. The reader can't tell how coverage is computed from the calibration, e.g. that Jev answers only when confident and the error is capped at 5%.

stumbles.quote: The bar set in advance was 50%.
stumbles.why: Introduced late and without saying what is measured. The opening says 'the bar set in advance' as if it were known. It is presumably the 50% settled fraction, but this is never stated.

stumbles.quote: At a 0.5 threshold the baseline also beat Jev on accuracy, 0.751 to 0.732.
stumbles.why: It's unclear which Jev variant (with or without the definition) has 0.732. 'Also beat Jev' sits oddly after the AUROC figures, where the baseline (0.769) beat only the no-definition Jev (0.697) and lost to the definition one (0.808).

stumbles.quote: Jev will not review declaude_lint's hits on public posts.
stumbles.why: 'declaude_lint' is not explained, and 'Oskar' and 'our public posting review process' are not introduced. The reader doesn't know what the lint does or who the people are.

stumbles.quote: It ranks the hits better than chance, but
stumbles.why: This sits uneasily with the later finding that a trivial category baseline ranks nearly as well (0.769 vs 0.808). The point of comparison is not made explicit.

point: Jev, a small calibrated decision model, ranked lint hits fairly well (AUROC 0.808) but was too poorly calibrated to settle even half of the hits at a 5% error rate (24.5% against a 50% bar), so it won't be added to public-post review.
